rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Adaptations of organisms to environmental conditions ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Adaptations of organisms to environmental conditions** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Organisms and Environment fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  An **adaptation** is any heritable trait — structural, physiological or behavioural — that improves an organism's survival and reproduction in its habitat. Natural selection builds them over generations: desert plants, high-altitude humans and deep-sea fish all carry solutions to the same problem (living where conditions are harsh) reached by different routes.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Desert adaptations: thick cuticle/succulence (cactus CAM photosynthesis — stomata open at night), long roots, reduced leaves (spines); animals: kangaroo rat uses metabolic water, nocturnal habits — pair plant + animal.  ·  Trick 2: Aquatic adaptations: floating leaves (water lily broad, waxy), hollow stems (buoyancy), air bladders in fish, webbed feet — the hydrophyte set.

rows.text: **Worked example — the kangaroo rat.** It lives in deserts without drinking water. Solutions: (1) physiological — its kidneys produce urine far more concentrated than ours; (2) metabolic — water released when fats are oxidised covers its needs; (3) behavioural — it stays in a cool burrow by day and feeds at night,…  ·  ## 7.
